title: Loss Functions — Choose a Loss That Matches the Output
key_insight: Mean squared error averages squared numeric misses. Cross-entropy rewards high probability on the correct class and strongly penalizes confident wrong answers.
body:
## Choose a Loss That Matches the Output

A house-price model predicts numbers, while an image model chooses among classes. Using one loss for both gives the outputs the wrong interpretation.

Mean squared error averages squared numeric misses. Cross-entropy rewards high probability on the correct class and strongly penalizes confident wrong answers.

Libraries often combine a final transformation with the loss for numerical safety. Read whether the function expects raw scores or probabilities before adding your own activation.
common_mistakes: Loss is only a chart and never affects training.
The largest possible loss always means the best model.
One loss has the correct meaning for every output type.
mini_exercise: Sketch the situation in “Choose a Loss That Matches the Output” as three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Training needs a meaningful numeric objective before it can decide how weights should change.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “Choose a Loss That Matches the Output” situation, explain Loss Functions without assuming the listener knows deep learning.
